questions.stem: What is the profit margin of a shopkeeper who buys a geometry box for ₹75 and sells it for ₹110?
questions.solution: The profit margin is calculated as the difference between the selling price and the cost price. Here, the shopkeeper sells the geometry box for ₹110 and buys it for ₹75. The profit is 110 - 75 = ₹35. Therefore, the profit margin is ₹35. The other options are incorrect because they represent the cost price, selling price, or the difference between the two, but not the actual profit.

hi.stem: एक दुकानदार ₹75 में एक ज्यामिति बॉक्स खरीदता है और इसे ₹110 में बेचता है। लाभ अंक क्या है?
hi.solution: लाभ अंक की गणना बिक्री मूल्य और लागत मूल्य के अंतर के रूप में की जाती है। यहां, दुकानदार ज्यामिति बॉक्स को ₹110 में बेचता है और ₹75 में खरीदता है। लाभ 110 - 75 = ₹35 है। अतः, लाभ अंक ₹35 है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे लागत मूल्य, बिक्री मूल्य या दोनों के अंतर का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं, लेकिन वास्तविक लाभ नहीं है।

questions.stem: If a carpenter wants a profit margin of 50% on a chair that costs ₹475, at what price should he sell the chair?
questions.solution: To achieve a 50% profit margin, the selling price must be 150% of the cost price. The cost price is ₹475, so the selling price is 475 × 1.5 = ₹712.5. The other options are incorrect because they represent the cost price, double the cost price (which would be 100% profit), or half the cost price (which would be a loss).

hi.solution: 50% लाभ अर्जित करने के लिए, बिक्री मूल्य लागत मूल्य के 150% होना चाहिए। लागत मूल्य ₹475 है, इसलिए बिक्री मूल्य 475 × 1.5 = ₹712.5 है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वे लागत मूल्य, दोगुना लागत मूल्य (जो 100% लाभ होगा) या आधा लागत मूल्य (जो नुकसान होगा) का प्रतिनिधित्व करते हैं।

questions.solution: A percentage represents a part per hundred, so 24% is equivalent to 24 out of 100, which is 24/100. The other options do not represent 24 parts per 100; 24/50 equals 48%, 24/25 equals 96%, and 24/10 equals 240%.

questions.stem: If 25% of a quantity is 50, what is the full quantity?
questions.solution: If 25% of a quantity equals 50, then 25% is equivalent to 25/100 or 1/4 of the quantity. To find the full quantity, multiply 50 by 4, which gives 200. The correct answer is 200. Other options are incorrect because 250 would require 20% to be 50, 500 would require 10% to be 50, and 100 would mean 50 is 50%, which doesn't match the given 25%.

questions.stem: If 40% of a distance is 92 km, what is 60% of the same distance?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 138 km. Since 40% of the distance is 92 km, 20% would be 46 km, and therefore 60% (which is 3 times 20%) would be 138 km. The other options are incorrect because they do not follow the proportional relationship between the percentages and the distances.

questions.stem: The price of 1 kg tomatoes increased from ₹30 to ₹42. What is the percentage increase in price?
questions.solution: The increase in price is ₹42 - ₹30 = ₹12. To find the percentage increase, we calculate (12/30) × 100 = 40%. The correct answer is 40%. 30% is the original price as a percentage, 50% is an incorrect calculation, and 20% is a miscalculation of the increase.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper initially set the price of a product with a 35% profit margin. Due to poor sales, he decided to offer a 30% discount on the selling price. Will he make a profit or a loss?
questions.solution: If the shopkeeper sets the price with a 35% profit margin, the selling price is 135% of the cost. A 30% discount on this price reduces it to 70% of 135%, which is 94.5% of the cost. This means he makes a loss. The other options are incorrect because he does not make a profit, he does not break even, and the result can be determined.

hi.solution: यदि दुकानदार ने 35% लाभ के मार्जिन के साथ कीमत निर्धारित की, तो बिक्री मूल्य लागत का 135% होगा। इस कीमत पर 30% की छूट लागत के 70% के 135% तक कम हो जाती है, जो लागत के 94.5% के बराबर होता है। इसका अर्थ है कि वह हानि कमाता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि वह लाभ नहीं कमाता है, वह बराबरी नहीं करता है, और परिणाम निर्धारित किया जा सकता है।

questions.stem: Nandini has 25 marbles, of which 15 are white. What percentage of her marbles are white?
questions.solution: To find the percentage of white marbles, we use the formula: (number of white marbles / total marbles) × 100. So, (15/25) × 100 = 60%. Therefore, the correct answer is 60%.
